thread:
maya: quick sync — we saw a lease handoff race in staging during the canary restart, want to align on fix before I ship the refactor
aj: saw the alert. Two nodes briefly believed they owned the same prefix and both served cached KV for a few dozen seconds
lina: was this during heavy load or just the rolling reboot?
maya: rolling reboot + synthetic load spike. lease renewals overlapped while compactor moved slabs
sven: root cause I can reproduce: compactor's aggressive slab compaction invalidated prefetched keys while the lease state remained valid in-memory. node A had a stale partial cache but still considered itself owner
danielle: this is the classic tradeoff from the original design: minimal global coord for handoff in exchange for faster path, but now compaction changed invariants
aj: eviction path never checked for 'transferring' state. compactor moved entries out from under an ongoing transfer
maya: two options in my head:
- make the handoff durable (persist a transfer marker) so anyone can detect in-progress transfers
- or make compactor lease-aware so it won't compact slabs involved in transfers
sven: durable markers buy correctness but cost RPCs on handoff. for heavy canary traffic that could worsen tail latency
lina: lease-aware compaction avoids extra RPCs but risks blocking eviction indefinitely if a transfer hangs
danielle: how about a hybrid: write a lightweight transfer token to metadata store (cheap write) to make in-progress handoffs visible; compactor checks local token cache before evicting. token TTL keeps blocks bounded
aj: sketch token = {prefix, from, to, epoch, tenancy}. small idempotent write; sequencer could optionally provide ordering if needed
maya: handshake pattern I'd propose:
```
1) A prepares transfer to B, writes transfer-token(prefix,P->B,epoch)
2) A signals B and streams a thin snapshot or enables B to lazy-fetch
3) B starts serving in 'warming' mode (misses cause fetches)
4) B marks token complete when warm / snapshot done
5) A clears local blocking and normal eviction resumes
```
lina: streaming full snapshots is heavy for large prefixes. prefer lazy fill + prioritized background prefetch based on recent heatmap
sven: agreed. warming mode increases first-request P99; background prefetch policy needs to be tunable by prefix size and current QPS
danielle: multi-tenant nuance: shared pools may serve overlapping prefixes across tenants. tokens must be namespaced by tenant and enforce isolation
aj: boundary question: where to store tokens? sequencer gives linearization but is heavier. lease-manager already manages lease lifecycle and is lightweight
maya: proposal: lease-manager owns token lifecycle but sequencer can create a transfer-ticket idempotently when strict ordering is requested. default path: lease-manager token writes to central metadata store with short TTL
sven: compactor change: check local metadata cache for transfer tokens before compaction; if token present, block compaction of affected slabs. also surface metric active_transfer_blocked_slabs
lina: safety rules we must prove empirically: at-most-one-full-owner at steady state; no silent stale-serving after token completion. bounded overlap allowed during transfer but must be observable
aj: test matrix:
- chaos: kill the source node mid-transfer, assert no two nodes have full-resident cache for same prefix
- perf: measure added tail for token writes on canary handoffs
- stress: high churn handoffs with small prefixes + aggressive compaction
- correctness: detect any stale_serves via eval harness and compare outputs from two replicas
danielle: metrics to add: transfer_attempts, transfer_success, transfer_fail, transfer_duration_ms, blocked_slab_count, stale_serves_detected
maya: rollout plan:
1) implement token write in lease-manager behind feature flag (TTL=0 default)
2) enable for limited canary prefixes and collect metrics
3) enable compactor checks in canary with per-prefix blocking limits
4) if stable, widen rollout
5) gate on stale_serves_detected < 0.1% over 1h
sven: recovery ops: expose admin API to force-complete or abort stuck transfers; also an operator probe that alerts on tokens > threshold age
lina: add an automated remediation that attempts a best-effort abort then notifies oncall if abort fails
aj: I'll prototype token schema and a small bench for the metadata store write latency this afternoon
sven: I'll add token-check hook into compactor and a metric for blocked slabs
maya: great. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up capturing the hybrid approach and the rollout checklist, and open the prototype PR. please attach the chaos tests to the PR
infra-bot: deploy pipeline queued for rama/kv-transfer-token-prototype (canary)
maya: thanks. if we see stale_serves_detected > 0.2% in 15m window we rollback and iterate
danielle: logging note: emit token lifecycle events to distributed trace so we can correlate handoff latency with P99s
lina: +1. also add a debug endpoint to dump tokens and related slab ids for a prefix
aj: will do. ping me for prototype review
maya: moving to implementation, will share PR link and tests. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
